claim_verbatim: The US is preparing to shrink its debt by revaluing its gold and holding savers’ returns below inflation, and it has hired the authors of both plans to do it.
context: Opening line (standfirst) of the essay, under the title 'Warsh and Bessent Are Building a New Treasury-Fed Accord to Revalue America’s Gold'. The essay names Judy Shelton (Counselor to the Treasury Secretary from 9 Oct 2026; gold-convertible bond and gold revaluation) and David Zervos (Counselor; financial repression) as the authors of the two plans, and Paul Winfree in Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's office.
source: Substack essay 'Warsh and Bessent Are Building a New Treasury-Fed Accord to Revalue America’s Gold', ctindale.substack.com, 2 Nov 2026 12:04 UTC (2 Nov 2026 23:04 AEDT); also posted as X article https://x.com/ctindale/status/2117235154095833464 (2 Nov 2026 12:39 UTC)
mechanism: Revaluation of US government gold above the $42.22 statutory book price plus financial repression (savers' real returns held below inflation) to shrink the real debt burden, run through a new Treasury-Fed accord.
notes: Logged 3 Nov 2026 (within a day of publication). Declarative wording read as 'will' (0.90) under SCORING.md. No date or deadline is given, so it stays in the ledger as unscorable and is not queued in inferred-to-confirm.csv. Checkable events it points to: a change to the $42.22/oz statutory gold price or a mark-to-market of US gold on the government's books. Related: pl-104 (announcement of this essay), pl-110. Quoted as published.

claim_verbatim: Of course, what he said in an essay in 2023 doesn't make it about to happen today; it just raises the odds considerably. Treasury now employs Judy Shelton, who designed the gold-convertible bond, and the Fed chair’s office employs Paul Winfree, who wrote the Project 2025 Federal Reserve chapter that calls for that bond. These are the people you hire when you intend to issue the bond.
context: Free half of the 2 Nov 2026 gold essay, after describing Winfree's 2023 Project 2025 Fed chapter (free banking under which 'the Federal Reserve is effectively abolished'; 'gold-convertible Treasury instruments'). Later in the same essay: Shelton expected a maiden issue 'say, on July 4, 2026' to be oversubscribed; '4 Jul 2026 has passed without that Treasury offering. The offering is the signal to watch.'
